messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: name-mangling for model variables
parts:
We'll do the mangling for model variable names. It
seems like the easiest way to get backward compatibility
for new function names.

I just really really want to get 2.0 out before heading
off in new directions. So I don't want to make this
change before then.

- Bob

On 10/9/13 12:23 PM, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
> It's a useful quantity to have around, although it's easy to work around if
> there isn't a specific function for it. (Although that's true of all the
> numerical constants...)
>
> I'm indifferent to whether you get rid of it or rename it. If renaming it,
> I'd suggest eps(), which is used by Matlab, or machine_precision() if eps()
> is too terse.
>
> That said, it would be really nice if variables didn't have to conflict
> with function names but that seems like a bigger and harder problem.
>
>

> > That seems more harmful than good.

messages.author: 2a7f346506a3e9ff
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] name-mangling for model variables
parts: I agree, I'd say variable name mangling can wait until 2.0 is out the door.
On Wed, Oct 9, 2013 at 1:32 PM, Bob Carpenter <ca...@alias-i.com> wrote:

We'll do the mangling for model variable names.  It
seems like the easiest way to get backward compatibility
for new function names.

I just really really want to get 2.0 out before heading
off in new directions.  So I don't want to make this
change before then.

- Bob

On 10/9/13 12:23 PM, Marcus Brubaker wrote:
It's a useful quantity to have around, although it's easy to work around if
there isn't a specific function for it. (Although that's true of all the
numerical constants...)

I'm indifferent to whether you get rid of it or rename it. If renaming it,
I'd suggest eps(), which is used by Matlab, or machine_precision() if eps()
is too terse.

That said, it would be really nice if variables didn't have to conflict
with function names but that seems like a bigger and harder problem.
